name: Azodicarbonamide
what_is: A flour-treatment and dough-conditioning ingredient used in specified food applications in the United States.
why_botia: BOTIA flags an explicit azodicarbonamide declaration because FDA lists it for specified direct food uses and, as of 2026, is conducting a post-market reassessment. Being under review does not itself mean the ingredient has been found unsafe, and BOTIA does not infer it when it is absent from the label.
can_1: Detect azodicarbonamide and common abbreviations or chemical synonyms when explicitly declared.
can_2: Show the current U.S. regulatory and reassessment context without converting review status into a hazard claim.
cannot_1: Determine the amount used or the concentrations of reaction products after baking.
cannot_2: Assume that bread, flour or dough contains azodicarbonamide when it is not listed.
